name: functional-justified-recovery
description: R9 companion: preserve necessary bounded recovery in a correct normalization change. Stage outside a SKILL.md ancestor; run standard and actual isolated workflows.
prompt: I've staged the preference ID normalization change. Run `$kk:review-code` against it.
trap: A simplification recommendation can remove the unchanged retry mechanism required by the explicit contract.

assertions.text: The main actor completes applicable review instructions and resolved profile reads before behavioral investigation; isolated children load supplied methodology before analyzing evidence. Distinguish bounded routing from behavioral reads.
The review traces Preferences.read through normalized keys and Repository.read_resilient, explaining that trimming and the existing bounded transient-recovery contract are both preserved.

The assessment covers transient-then-success, three exhausted transient failures and an immediate permanent MissingPreference error; it distinguishes actual executions from source inspection and attributes any supplied test evidence.

The review does not recommend replacing read_resilient with read_once, removing retry machinery, retrying permanent errors or otherwise simplifying away the required guarantee. Any alternative must preserve normalization and bounded recovery.

The report approves the scoped compatible change without invented blockers, mandatory new abstraction/locking/deployment gates or unsupported production guarantees, and names the inspected paths and evidence limits.

In isolated mode actual named-reviewer and PAL dispatches carry the diff, explicit README contract and relevant unchanged callers/state source; retain both results and disclose missing source coverage. Standard mode does not require independent dispatches.
